the_rebase_lost_nothing.detail: Verified independently and by path classification rather than by trusting a summary, because a rebase on this branch dropped three files once before. The set of files the branch touches is identical pre- and post-rebase except for the addition of this witness's third record: comm -23 of the two name lists is empty. Every content difference between 3b1b578 and 5faaf5b is then accounted for: thirteen paths are files main changed between d00f46a and 48a0f57 (the CI workflows, retention.py, workflows.py, three test modules and five CI-retention observation records), and the remainder are exactly the files the two new commits target. Nothing is unexplained. Records 1 and 2 are byte-identical across the rebase, and record 3 as committed matches this witness's on-disk bytes exactly.

the_withdrawal_is_complete_in_what_it_gr.detail: No kind, contract clause or fixture for the withdrawn kinds survives in anything that runs. standing_vocabulary, retired_identifiers and representation_rule are all gone from the contract; coverage now holds derived (CAPABILITY, REFERENCE, STANDING, SELFCLAIM), presence_only (PROVENANCE) and a not_covered list of six. kinds() reports 5 and the contract describes exactly those 5. The withdrawal is recorded rather than silent: not_covered's first entry names the two kinds, the date, the failing example pair - 'accepted but unbuilt' refused while 'implementation is still pending' passed - and the SDLC.md Red/Blue rationale, and a successor clause names the concern and two routes.

the_shape_based_coverage_read_is_not_vac.detail: This was the specific risk asked about and the reading is not vacuous. Emptying coverage entirely fires, naming all five kinds as undescribed. Converting derived from a mapping to a list fires, naming the four kinds that group held. Removing every group and leaving only not_covered fires. So removing a group cannot silently stop the grading; it turns every kind in it into a named defect. The inverse also holds: adding an unrelated mapping under coverage is read as a kind group and fires 'the contract describes [author]'. That is arguably correct authoring feedback rather than a false positive, but it is an undeclared constraint - coverage may contain only kind mappings plus list-shaped prose - and the contract does not say so.

the_three_generalization_fixtures_hold_t.detail: They do, and not incidentally. The shipped values are genuinely absent from every list: Kubernetes, contracts/quarterly-plan.yaml and banana_service_status each appear zero times across contracts/ and STATUS.yaml. More to the point, the property holds for values this witness invented after reading the code: tool 'Zygomorphic' and tool 'PowerShell7' are refused CAPABILITY, address contracts/xyzzy-plough.toml is refused REFERENCE, subject aardvark_service_status is refused STANDING, and a novel token FLABBERGASTED on a real subject is refused STANDING. The mechanism is why: CAPABILITY is an allow-list so anything outside it fails, REFERENCE is an index lookup, STANDING is a record lookup. Three negative controls confirm the fixture does not simply refuse everything - a valid tool set, a valid tracked address and a true status claim are each silent. That is the discriminating test the earlier phrase experiment failed.

STANDING_belongs_with_the_four_rather_th.detail: Answered as asked, and the answer is that it belongs with the four, but it is the weakest of the five and the reason it belongs is narrower than 'it generalizes'. The dividing line is not how much a kind generalizes; it is whether a record other than the check itself decides the verdict. VOLATILE and RETIRED had no oracle - the nine-string list WAS the standard, so the list defined the offence and anything unlisted was not an offence at all. STANDING has an oracle in STATUS.yaml: its regex is a recognizer, not the standard, and once a claim is extracted the verdict comes from a record, which is why a subject and a token nobody ever wrote are both refused. Its narrowness is real and should not be understated: of six spellings of one false claim, only the canonical 'subject_status is TOKEN' is caught; the colon form 'asset_service_status: WITNESSED' is missed, as are 'is now', '=', and two prose restatements. The contract does say 'ONLY matches that one sentence form', which is honest. The cheap improvement is to widen the recognizer to the obvious separators, and that is categorically different from extending a phrase list, because widening a recognizer changes what is extracted while the judgement stays with STATUS.yaml, whereas extending the withdrawn lists changed what counted as an offence.

the_withdrawal_left_no_residue_in_the_ar.detail: Two pieces of residue survive, both in scripts/sov_harness.py and neither affecting a verdict. First, dead code: the DESCRIPTION regex at line 62 and the _described() helper at line 94 existed only to serve check_volatile, and a repository-wide search finds exactly one reference to _described, its own definition. Neither is called by any member of ALL_CHECKS. Second, and the one that matters more for a tool of this kind, the module docstring at lines 30 to 31 still tells the reader that a description 'does not state standing, which is the one representation rule the contract imposes and the remedy is always deletion'. The contract imposes no such rule any more: representation_rule appears zero times in contracts/ and zero times in scripts/, and the code that enforced it was check_volatile. So the module asserts a contract clause that no longer exists and a remedy nothing applies. The substance is disclosed correctly one file away, in not_covered's first entry, which makes this a stale sentence rather than a false coverage claim - but it is an unsupported claim about a record, in the artifact whose entire purpose is refusing those.
